author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: The infant's survival immediately after birth was highly uncertain. Had he died early, his life story would have been brief but accurate.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: The child struggled to take his first breath. Fortunately, there were no skilled doctors or worried relatives around, so Nature and a drunk workhouse nurse were able to keep him alive.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: The baby cried for the first time, drawing the attention of his dying mother on a nearby bed.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: The mother kissed her newborn baby and died right away while the surgeon watched coldly.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: The surgeon observed the dead mother and professionally noted that she had passed away.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: The drunken nurse agreed with the surgeon, but was more focused on finding her hidden alcohol bottle.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: The surgeon told the nurse to feed the baby if it cried, and casually wondered where the attractive mother came from.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: The nurse said the mother was found collapsed in the street, having walked far, but nobody knew her origin.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: The surgeon noticed the dead woman had no wedding ring and dismissed her as a common unmarried mother.

author: Charles Dickens
ai_plain_text: The surgeon went to dinner while the nurse drank from her bottle and started dressing the baby.
